quote: We aim to examine one critical question that has been overlooked in GCE works: 'Although LLM-enriched captions boost VLM performance, do they have negative effects, regarding societal bias and object hallucination?' ... Our analysis reveals that LLM-enriched captions indeed have negative side effects...

We analyze concise (COCO captions) and enriched captions (ShareGPT4V, FuseCap, Caps‑Fusion) based on the metrics in Section 2.2. ... This analysis focuses on caption quality, societal bias, and hallucination.
Improving training paradigms and data augmentation strategies are crucial topics to enhance VLM performance in image captioning.
We introduce the metrics to evaluate each aspect. ... Vocabulary diversity ... Caption length ... Recall ... Gender error ... Recall disparity ... LIC ... CHAIR ...

We evaluate caption quality in three aspects: Vocabulary diversity ... Caption length ... Recall ... We adopt three metrics to measure gender bias: Gender error, Recall disparity, LIC ... We use the CHAIR metric to evaluate hallucination.

We evaluate caption quality in three aspects: Vocabulary diversity is the total number of unique words across all captions in D. Caption length is the average number of tokens per caption in D. Recall measures the proportion of objects mentioned in captions to the total objects in the images.
